target_customer: Small lawn care and landscaping businesses in the US and Canada that pay for management software
problem: Small landscaping companies run scheduling, estimates, invoices and payments on paper or spreadsheets. Yardbook offers software to run the business end to end.
business_model: SaaS subscription for landscapers (a marketplace was pitched in 2016 coverage)
product_category: Field service software for lawn care

founders.name: Mark Ke
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (2016-02-10) describes him as having left Yahoo to start the company.

founders.name: Brian Gamido
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in the TechCrunch article of 2016-02-10 (via search snippet); not listed on the YC page.

competitors.name: Lawn Love
competitors.what: Online marketplace for lawn care launched from YC Summer 2014
competitors.funding_then: A 2014-11 VentureBeat headline reports a $1.9M raise

technical_complexity.rationale: Scheduling, invoicing and payments for small businesses are standard web application work.

defensibility.rationale: Many similar landscaping tools exist and switching costs are low for small operators.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Lawn Love was acquired by LawnStarter in August 2021 per CB Insights; Yardbook itself was not acquired and is still operating in 2026.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in February 2016 framed it around a $30.9 billion US lawn care industry of small operators.

branding.domain_note: Uses yardbook.com, the exact .com; a USPTO record shows first use November 2013 and a June 2014 filing.

brand_strength.rationale: Clear descriptive compound name with an exact .com, but no press or community about the brand was found.

outcome_analysis: Yardbook joined YC in Winter 2016 and appears to have stayed small and independent, with about 7 employees in late 2024 per Latka and software listings still updated in 2026. No outside funding beyond a reported small YC seed was found, and no acquisition or shutdown. The company looks like a durable niche tool rather than a venture-scale outcome, though the available data are thin.
notes: CB Insights lists a seed of about $120K from Y Combinator on 2016-03-23; single aggregator, so not recorded as a round. Founding year conflicts: Seedtable and CB Insights say 2014, Latka says 2016; trademark first use is 2013. The company site returned HTTP 403 so it could not be read. A CB Insights comparison page shows Acquired for Yardbook but that appears to be a data error from Lawn Love's data; a separate CB Insights profile says Alive. LawnStarter, LMN and Jobber appear as rivals only on undated pages and are not listed.
